findings.title: A widely cited cost figure for Google's security assessment is out of date
findings.detail: A 2019 article, updated in 2021, cites $15,000 to $75,000. That predates the CASA framework. The most recent public figure found is about $540 per app for Tier 2 (2024). The guide shows both with their dates and lists the current price as unverified.

findings.title: Conflicting reports on the Client ID limit were resolved from Spotify's own guide
findings.detail: The February 2026 announcement set one Client ID per developer. A third-party article said 25. Spotify's migration guide confirms the limit was raised to 25 in July 2026. The guide records the change and the conflict.

findings.title: Ten Gmail quotes failed the first check because Google served a translated page
findings.detail: Without a language header, Google sometimes redirected the fetcher to a machine-translated Arabic version of its documentation, so English quotes could not match. The fetcher now requests English. After the fix, all 105 library quotes matched.

findings.title: The agent matched a nonsense query to an unrelated product
findings.detail: Given a made-up name, the first version picked a real product from the search results and wrote a guide for it. The agent now states whether the query refers to a real product and stops with a clear message when it does not.

findings.title: Posts on a provider's own forum were graded as official documentation
findings.detail: In the first Strava run, community forum posts on a Strava domain were treated as official. Forum and community hosts are now graded as community evidence even on the provider's domain.

findings.title: The agent chose a private-app path as the default
findings.detail: In the first Pipedrive run, the headline described the public route (weeks) while the main figure showed the private route (1 to 2 days). The default path is now the one that lets users outside the developer's organisation connect.

findings.title: Whether existing Slack installations lost their rate-limit exemption in March 2026
findings.detail: Secondary sources report a 3 March 2026 cut-off. The Slack changelog page read for the guide states only that existing installations were not affected. The guide marks the later date as a community report.

findings.title: Typical review time for sensitive scopes
findings.detail: Google states up to 10 days. Vendor articles state 3 to 5 business days and 2 to 4 weeks. The guide uses Google's figure and does not rely on the vendor figures.

findings.title: Time to verify a new Microsoft partner account
findings.detail: Microsoft states that publisher verification completes in minutes once prerequisites are met. No source read gives the time to verify a new partner account, so the guide's 1 to 7 day wait is labelled as an estimate.

findings.title: Terms on using API data with AI models
findings.detail: The developer terms for Spotify and Microsoft Graph were not read. Both guides list this as unverified.

findings.title: The automated check misses discovery documents at non-standard paths
findings.detail: It looks at standard locations on common hosts. GitHub's and Microsoft's documents sit elsewhere, so those two entries were completed from manual requests.

findings.title: Effort estimates are judgement, not sourced
findings.detail: Providers publish review times but not the developer's own effort. Every active-effort range in the library is labelled as an estimate.
